reproduction_target: Re-derive the paper's results: (a) the simulation-study performance figures (sensitivity/specificity of recombinant detection, position-by-position ancestry accuracy, parental-lineage-pair recovery, breakpoint-distance) on 1,000 synthetic recombinants + 1,000 controls, and (b) the empirical analysis of 440,307 GenBank SARS-CoV-2 sequences from England (Sep 2020 - Mar 2024): per-test-window recombinant proportion, its association with ONS community prevalence, observed-vs-expected recombinant counts by parental lineage pair, and the genome-wide breakpoint distribution.
granularity_note: Stage-1 prose triage. Steps derived from Materials and methods sections 2.1-2.10 plus the Implementation section (one step per named tool/analysis invocation). No workflow file (Snakefile/CWL/Nextflow/WDL/Makefile) was observed at the repository root, so the workflow-file anchor was unavailable; the repo landing page shows only directories (HMM_manuscript/, analyze-real-data-results/, analyze-sim-results/, data/, envs/, run-on-cluster/, sim/) plus .gitattributes, .gitignore and README.md. Repo source was NOT read (Stage-2 scope). |S| = 11 computational steps, |W| = 0.

steps.label: Obtain SARS-CoV-2 sequences and metadata from GenBank, processed using the Nextstrain pipeline (Methods 2.1)

Filter to sequences collected in England Sep 2020 - Mar 2024 and iteratively collapse Pango lineages with <10,000 sequences into the parental (unaliased) lineage; 2,304 lineages -> 41 collapsed lineages incl. 'other' (Methods 2.1)

Build 185 sliding reference/test window pairs (43-day window advanced by 7 days; first 36 days = reference, last 7 days = test) with random subsampling to 100,000 reference / 3,000 test sequences (Methods 2.2)
Compute the per-position nucleotide frequency matrix for each of the 185 reference sets (non-ACGT excluded; uniform 0.25 fallback when a lineage has no standard base at a position) (Methods 2.3)

Per-test-sequence maximum-likelihood estimation of the HMM parameters lambda (reparameterised as tau) and pseudo-frequency epsilon, using a custom O(M) forward algorithm and scipy.optimize.minimize (L-BFGS-B); init (log eps, tau) = (log 0.005, 1); bounds log eps in [log 1e-8, log 0.02], tau in [0, 3] (Methods 2.5-2.6, Implementation)
Viterbi decoding of the most likely local Pango lineage ancestry per test sequence at the MLE parameters; classify a sequence as recombinant if the path contains >=1 lineage transition (Methods 2.7)

Simulation-data generation: 500 one-breakpoint + 500 two-breakpoint synthetic recombinants and 1,000 controls drawn from the 14,599-sequence reference set (England, 6 Nov - 11 Dec 2022), with mutation counts drawn from an empirical per-branch substitution distribution (n=567; median 2, IQR 1-4, mean 3.45, range 1-70) (Methods 2.8)

Simulation evaluation: sensitivity/specificity, mean position-by-position ancestry accuracy, parental lineage / lineage-pair recovery rate, 95% exact binomial CIs, 500-replicate nonparametric bootstrap CIs, logistic regression of detection on parental Hamming distance, and breakpoint-distance summaries (Methods 2.8)

Empirical analysis of 440,307 test-set sequences: per-7-day-window recombinant proportion, compared with window-averaged community prevalence from the UK ONS Coronavirus Infection Survey (Methods 2.9)

Expected-recombinant-count model: least-squares regression of the estimated recombinant proportion on the co-infection predictor to estimate theta and phi, then observed-vs-expected detected recombinant counts per parental lineage pair and the aggregated genome-wide breakpoint distribution (Methods 2.9-2.10)
Results-file processing and figure generation in R version 4.4.1 (Implementation)

gaps.missing: No accession list, no sequence-identifier table and no snapshot date/version for the 440,307 test sequences, the 185 reference/test window pairs, or the 14,599-sequence simulation reference set. The paper names GenBank (ref 16) and the Nextstrain-curated pipeline (ref 17) as the source but deposits no identifier for the exact extract used.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the accession list (or the Nextstrain metadata TSV with strain/accession + collection date) and state the download date of the curated snapshot.

gaps.where: Implementation section; all Python and R steps (S2-S11)
gaps.missing: 2a - Only the interpreter runtimes are pinned (Python 3.12.2, R 4.4.1). No versions for scipy/numpy or any R package, no channel/index, no declared platform, no lockfile in prose. The Nextstrain pipeline (S1) and the pangolin/pango-designation alias key used for lineage unaliasing (ref 18, Methods 2.1) carry no version at all.
gaps.how_to_close: Ship a conda-lock / pixi.lock / renv.lock (or a recorded image digest) declaring interpreter, package source and platform; state the ncov pipeline commit and the pango alias-key version.

gaps.where: Methods 2.2 (100,000 / 3,000 random subsampling), 2.8 (synthetic sequence generation, mutation-position sampling, 500-replicate bootstraps)
gaps.missing: No RNG seed is stated for any stochastic step. The simulation set, the per-window subsamples and the bootstrap CIs are therefore only distributionally, not exactly, reproducible.
gaps.how_to_close: State (and show as consumed) the RNG seeds, or deposit the generated synthetic sequence set and the subsampled window membership lists.

gaps.missing: The upstream curation/alignment of GenBank sequences is externalised to 'the Nextstrain pipeline' (ref 17) with no configuration, no build, no version and no copy in the authors' repository. The aligned-genome coordinate system that all downstream steps assume is produced entirely outside the deposited code.
gaps.how_to_close: Pin the ncov workflow commit and include the build config, or deposit the resulting alignment/metadata.

gaps.where: Methods 2.1 (Nextstrain-curated GenBank snapshot), Methods 2.9 (ONS Coronavirus Infection Survey prevalence series)
gaps.missing: Both external resources are obtained out-of-band. The ONS prevalence series is cited only as a journal reference (ref 21, Pouwels et al. 2021 Lancet Public Health) with no data URL, DOI or release date; the GenBank/Nextstrain snapshot has no date or version. Whether the code pins either resource is unverified at Stage 1 (env_capture_class deliberately left 'n/a'; class A/B/C requires the Stage-2 code read).
gaps.how_to_close: Give a versioned DOI/URL for the ONS release and a dated snapshot identifier for the sequence set; fetch both via a pinned download rule in the workflow (class A).

gaps.missing: Code is public and linked but not archived or pinned: the paper cites a bare repository URL with no commit hash, no release/tag (repo landing page shows 33 commits and no releases), no Zenodo/Software Heritage DOI, and no LICENSE file. The referenced snapshot is mutable and the reuse terms are undeclared. The README is a single sentence ('Repository for HMM to detect recombinant SARS-CoV-2 sequences.') with no install, environment or run instructions.
gaps.how_to_close: Tag a release, archive it to Zenodo, cite the DOI (or at least the commit hash) in the Availability section, add a LICENSE and a README with environment and run instructions.
